title: Effect on the simulation state
$comment: An effect is NOT a state: it is a change applied to ONE variable of the state. Soil, climate and finances share this format; only 'target' changes. Effects are deterministic given their drawn values (see monte_carlo.json).

target.description: JSON Pointer to the changed variable, relative to the chain node (markov.json#/definitions/node).

operation.description: add: adds 'value' once. multiply: multiplies by 'value'. set: overwrites. rate: 'value' per day, multiplied by the days spent in the state/action.

unit.description: Unit of 'value'. For add/set it is the target unit; for rate it is target unit per day; multiply is dimensionless.

at.description: When a one-off effect (add/multiply/set) fires inside a state: on entry (e.g. sowing cost) or on exit (e.g. harvest revenue). Ignored for operation=rate, which accumulates over the whole stay, and for effects on transitions, which fire when the edge is crossed.

when.description: Conditions on the node (all must hold). Empty/absent = always applies.

bounds.description: Clamp applied to the target after the effect (e.g. N2 >= 0, 3 <= pH <= 9).

provenance.description: Where the number comes from, specific enough to check it: a file and field, a dataset and query, a paper or a rule. Example: 'PAM municipal, year pair 2005-2006'.

quantity.description: Fixed number or distribution. A distribution is drawn once per trajectory from the parameters stream, keyed by trajectory index and the effect's location in the contracts, so the same draw repeats in every scenario of a run.

params.description: normal/lognormal: mean, sd | uniform: min, max | triangular: min, mode, max | beta: alpha, beta

path.description: JSON Pointer into the node, like 'target'.

support.description: How much evidence stands behind a number. observed: counted or measured in our data for this place (e.g. PAM year pairs for Franca-SP). derived: computed by a stated rule from observed data or physics (e.g. phenological order, pedotransfer AWC). pooled: borrowed from similar places or crops because this row has too few observations. prior: an assumption or literature range used until data exists. Never upgrade a value's support without new evidence.
